meta.title: Operation of Vibratory Sieve Shaker in Pharmacognosy Laboratory

sections.purpose: To separate crude drug powders and plant materials into defined particle size fractions using mechanical vibration and standard test sieves as per Indian Pharmacopoeia (IP) and WHO sieve analysis requirements.
sections.scope: Applicable to Pharmacognosy laboratory for particle size analysis of crude drug powders, determination of powder fineness for standardization, and fractionation prior to extraction.
procedure: Select appropriate sieves from the IP/BP sieve series based on the required powder grade (e.g., coarse powder: No. 10/No. 44; fine powder: No. 85/No. 120).
Clean all sieves with a soft brush — remove any residual powder from previous use.
Inspect sieve mesh for damage, holes, or blocked apertures — replace damaged sieves.
Arrange sieves in descending order of aperture size (largest opening at top, smallest at bottom) with a collection pan at the base.
Stack and lock the sieve assembly securely in the clamps of the vibratory shaker.
Weigh the drug powder sample accurately (typically 50–100 g) and record the weight.
Place the powder on the topmost (largest aperture) sieve and cover with the lid.
Set the vibration amplitude and time: for pharmacopeial sieve analysis — 5 minutes at standard amplitude.
Switch on the vibratory sieve shaker and allow the full run to complete.
After completion, switch off and allow vibration to cease fully before opening.
Carefully remove the sieve stack and weigh the retained material on each sieve and in the collection pan.
Calculate the weight percentage retained on each sieve: % retained = (Weight on sieve / Total sample weight) × 100.
Plot the cumulative particle size distribution curve if required.
Determine powder grade per IP: Coarse (No. 10), Moderately Coarse (No. 22), Moderately Fine (No. 44), Fine (No. 85), Very Fine (No. 120).
Clean all sieves with a soft brush after use; wash if needed and dry completely before storage.
Record all sieve numbers, weights, and calculated results in the laboratory register.
precautions: Never use metal objects to clean sieve mesh — use only a soft natural-bristle brush.
Do not overload sieves — excessive material prevents proper sieving and gives inaccurate results.
Wear a dust mask when handling fine drug powders during loading and unloading.
Do not use worn or damaged sieves — apertures out of specification invalidate results.
Ensure the sieve stack is securely fastened before starting — loose sieves cause accidents and sample loss.
Allow the shaker to stop completely before removing sieves.
Store sieves in their individual protective containers when not in use — stacking without protection deforms the mesh.
Calibrate the sieve apertures annually using optical methods or reference wire gauges.
